approach: Flip `enabled` to false in athena.toml [job_plan] (one line). Rename and update the repo-config test in config.rs to assert planning off with caps unchanged. The existing test `with_planning_absent_or_off_the_invocations_are_the_producer_verifier_pair_only` in job_plan.rs already covers a change job with `enabled = false` making no planner or critic call, so it is reused unchanged. Add D135 to decisions.md (the next free number after D134), a short outcome paragraph at the end of section 9 of job-planning.md, and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing disabled-path test in job_plan.rs; do not edit that file.
decisions.reason: It already runs a full change job with [job_plan] enabled = false and asserts the invocations are exactly Reader, Producer, Verifier, with no job-plan or critique records. A duplicate would add nothing (small).

rejected.option: Add a new test that loads the repository athena.toml into the CLI fixture
rejected.why: Larger change. The config test proves the repo file parses with planning off, and the fixture test proves the off path.

decisions.choice: Rename the config test to the_repository_config_turns_job_planning_off_with_the_designs_caps and assert !plan.enabled with caps unchanged.
decisions.reason: The old name and assertion would be false. Keeping the caps assertions guards 'no other change' and keeps the table present for a new trial.

rejected.why: It would lose the check that the [job_plan] table still parses with its caps.

decisions.choice: Record the outcome as a new entry D135, leaving D110's text intact, and cross-reference D110.
decisions.reason: decisions.md is an append-only log, and D134 is the last entry. The new entry says the rule decided, the brain acted under Sri's delegation, and the override was taken at 51 jobs, below the decision point.

rejected.why: It rewrites history in an append-only log.

demonstrations.method: Run the updated config test and the existing disabled-path test.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-data the_repository_config_turns_job_planning_off && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan with_planning_absent_or_off
demonstrations.observes: Both pass. The config test shows the repository athena.toml parses with job_plan present, enabled false and caps 0.75/0.75/600/600/3. The CLI test shows a change job with planning off invokes only Reader, Producer and Verifier and writes no job-plan or critique file.
demonstrations.fails_without: If athena.toml still had enabled = true, the config test would fail on the enabled assertion. If the off path invoked a planner or critic, the invocation-list assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: A stale test that still asserts enabled == true would fail cargo test.

open_questions: The athena status numbers come from the request and cannot be re-measured here, so the entry cites them as given.

Whether any other test or doc says planning is on (for example a budget or boundary test reading athena.toml) was not fully searched. The producer should grep for `job_plan` and 'planning is on' and run the full suite.
